proposals.impact: lift open rate on Money Worship and Money Avoidance sequences toward Vigilance's 66.67% benchmark
proposals.observation: The Money Vigilance automation achieved a 66.67% open rate on 12 sends. The Money Worship automation sits at 37.5% on 16 sends and Money Avoidance at 52.63% on 19 sends. The gap between Vigilance and Worship is 29 percentage points. The most plausible cause is the subject line: Vigilance-type readers are primed to engage with precise, slightly anxious framing, and that register likely matches something in the Vigilance email's subject that the Worship subject line does not replicate. Worship readers are equally high-intent but the subject line is probably not meeting them where the script in their head actually runs.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the Money Worship sequence's first email subject line to match the honest, specific register that appears to be driving Vigilance opens. The current subject almost certainly promises aspiration or relief. Replace it with a line that names the quiet internal contradiction Money Worship readers actually live with: earning more, spending more, never feeling further ahead. No hype, no promise of a fix. One sentence that sounds like something only Joel could have written at 2am looking at a bank statement that should have felt good.
proposals.current_text: subject: You work hard for your money — here's how to make it work harder for you
proposals.new_text: subject: You earned more this year. Why does it feel exactly the same?

proposals.impact: restore daily publishing cadence after three consecutive CI failures left queue at 1 post
proposals.observation: Three GitHub workflow runs failed in the last 24 hours: Daily Blog Post (08:35), Funnel-Hack Digest (13:13), and Weekly Queue Topup (19:43). The content queue now holds exactly one post. At one post per day that means tomorrow's publish is the last scheduled piece before the queue runs dry. The Daily Blog Post CI failure is the most urgent because it is the workflow that should have replenished or published today. The queue number did not move, which suggests the failure happened before any write occurred. Joel needs a manually written post in the queue today so the site does not go dark tomorrow.
proposals.proposal: Write and commit one ready-to-publish blog post directly into the content queue. The post does not need to be long. It needs to be specific enough to pass the Sultanic test and targeted squarely at the ICP: the 28-year-old who earns £65k, has three direct debits set up, calls that "being sorted", and has not opened their pension dashboard since they enrolled. The CI failures blocking the automated workflows are a separate engineering problem. This proposal is the human override that keeps the publishing cadence intact while that gets diagnosed.
proposals.new_text:
---
title: "You set up the direct debits. Why does sorted still feel like a lie?"
pubDate: 2026-09-22
description: "The admin is done. The numbers move on payday. So why does the quiet dread not move with them?"
tags: [money behaviour, self-awareness, honest reckoning]
---

You did the responsible things. Pension enrolled at work. ISA set to drip in on the first of the month. Subscriptions audited once, eighteen months ago. By every surface measure, you are sorted.

The dread does not care about surface measures.

It turns up on a Sunday evening when you check your balance and feel nothing useful. Not alarmed, not relieved. Just a low hum that says: *this is probably fine and I have no idea if this is fine.*

That hum is not anxiety in the clinical sense. It is the gap between the system you built and the understanding you never quite got around to building underneath it.

Joel sat with a client last month who had £150k in a workplace pension she had never logged into. The contributions were correct. The fund was default. Everything was working. She described opening the provider app as something she kept meaning to do "when she had more headspace." She is 31. She has a postgraduate degree. She is not careless with money. She is just running a system she does not fully see, and somewhere below the direct debits, she knows it.

Sorted is a posture. It gets you through conversations at dinner where someone asks if you have an ISA.

The work underneath sorted is different. It is knowing what the pension is actually invested in. It is having a number in your head that means something, not just a percentage contribution that HR chose as the default. It is the quiet reckoning that comes when you stop outsourcing the understanding to the automation.

The direct debits are good. They are not enough on their own. At some point the tab has to be opened.

If you want to know what your money is actually doing, not what the system is doing on autopilot, that is the conversation Joel runs with clients one-to-one. MSc Behavioural Economics | Qualified Financial Planner.

proposals.impact: drive first quiz sessions after 48-hour zero-start window
proposals.observation: The quiz recorded zero sessions and zero starts across a 48-hour window. The homepage is the highest-traffic owned surface in the stack and almost certainly carries a quiz call-to-action somewhere in its hero or mid-page section. If the CTA copy is generic ("Take the quiz", "Find out your money type") it is doing no work for the 25-35 ICP who lands from search or social in a mild state of scepticism. A single line of friction-lowering, specific framing above or beside the CTA button can move cold traffic into quiz starts without any structural page change.
proposals.proposal: Sharpen the homepage quiz CTA by replacing the generic button label or surrounding teaser copy with a line that names the specific internal experience the ICP is arriving with. They are not looking for a money personality quiz. They are looking for a way to understand why the behaviour keeps repeating despite the intention being entirely sincere. The new copy should name that gap in one sentence, then let the button do the rest.
proposals.current_text: Take the quiz — find out your money personality type
proposals.new_text: You already know what you should do. This shows you why you keep not doing it.
